gaps.sentence: They ___ for two hours when the storm hit.
gaps.hint: two hours of walking before the storm
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous: had been walking.

gaps.sentence: The bus ___ at 6.40 tomorrow morning, according to the timetable.
gaps.hint: official timetables use the present simple
gaps.explanation: Official timetables take the present simple for future events: leaves.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time she ___ a car on her own.
gaps.hint: it was the first time takes past perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It was the first time' in past contexts, English uses the past perfect: had driven.

gaps.sentence: I can't talk now — I ___ dinner for twelve people.
gaps.hint: now plus a temporary activity in progress
gaps.explanation: 'Now' marks a temporary action in progress, so the present continuous is needed: am cooking.

gaps.sentence: I usually walk to work, but today I ___ the bus because it is raining.
gaps.hint: today contrasts with the usual habit
gaps.explanation: 'But today' signals a temporary break from habit, so the present continuous is correct: am taking.

gaps.sentence: It is the first time I ___ paella.
gaps.hint: it is the first time takes present perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It is the first time', English uses the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: By the end of the month, they ___ the new bridge.
gaps.hint: by the end of means completed before
gaps.explanation: An action completed before a specific future point takes the future perfect: will have finished.

gaps.sentence: Don't disturb him — he ___ an important video call with the client.
gaps.hint: do not disturb means it is happening now
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at the moment of speaking takes the present continuous: is having.
